earlier_scan.source_named: Only Koops 2007 Lufu word list (rogerblench.info, 403) and comparative Jukunoid classification works (Prischnegg 2008/2010/2021); no phonology or grammar of Lufu found.

sources.citation: Rennison, John R. Publication list (homepage.univie.ac.at/john.rennison/, Internet Archive copy 2026-01-29).
sources.note: No publication on Lufu; only Prischnegg & Rennison 2007 fieldwork report, Rennison 2014 on Yukuben vowel harmony, and 'A Grammar of Yukuben' (forthcoming).

sources.citation: Weitzenauer, Sabine Maria. 2008. Numerus in Nominalklassen in Niger-Congo Sprachen am Beispiel des Yukuben. Diplomarbeit, Universitaet Wien (utheses id 2064, DOI 10.25365/thesis.2419) -- full text searched via the utheses solr proxy.
sources.access_detail: read online, no copy. access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Lufu occurs only in the bibliography: 'Rennison, John R. & Tamara Prischnegg. 2008. Unveroeffentlichtes Sprachmaterial zum Bete, Kapya, Kuteb, Lufu, Shibong und Yukuben.. Ms. Wien.' Confirms primary Lufu data exist only as unpublished Vienna-project materials.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2026. Rethinking the classification of 'South Jukunoid'. Paper presented at Bantoid 3, University at Buffalo, 20-21 May 2026.
sources.note: Most recent synthesis of all South Jukunoid/Yukubenic data including Lufu; Blench's classification papers usually carry a short phonology note (vowels, tones) per language and name the wordlist sources (e.g. Koops).

sources.citation: Kempf, Viktoria & Tamara Prischnegg. 2020. A sketch of Akum (Southern Jukunoid). Afrika und Uebersee 93: 299-331. DOI 10.15460/auue.2020.93.1.215.
sources.note: Describes Akum, not Lufu (Lufu only named p.305 in a list of Southern Jukunoid languages sharing an unclear-status central vowel). Akum phonology: consonants, vowels, 2.3 Tone 'three-tone system'; no statement on stress/accent anywhere.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019/2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, edition IV. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation.
sources.note: Nothing. Front matter p.vi: Lufu 'not extinct, see entry' (the L-section of this edition contains no Lufu entry); classification appendix lists Lufu under Jukunoid > Yukuben-Kutep.

sources.citation: Pozdniakov, Konstantin. 2018. The numeral system of Proto-Niger-Congo: A step-by-step reconstruction (Niger-Congo Comparative Studies 2). Berlin: Language Science Press. Sec. 4.1.3.4 'Lufu', Table 4.53 'Lufu numerals' (p. 104); Appendix E Table E.27 'BC: isolates' (source for Lufu: Tamara Prischnegg, contributor for Chan 1998-2018).
sources.note: Second-hand numeral table with tone marks (ù-tí, (ba)-máhà, bá-tá, ba-ɲì, bá-tsó, ú-wó, e-ce); no phonology, tone-system or stress remark for Lufu anywhere in the book (13 'tone' hits, none about Lufu).

sources.citation: Chan, Eugene S. L. (comp.). 2013. 'Lufu, Taraba state, Nigeria'. In: Numeral Systems of the World's Languages (MPI-EVA lingweb). Linguist providing data and date: Dr. Tamara Prischnegg, Institut für Afrikawissenschaften, Universität Wien, 15 April 2013.
sources.note: Numerals 1-20 transcribed with tone diacritics (acute/grave: ùtí 1, (ba)máhà 2, bátá 3, baɲì 4, bátsó 5, bázó dʒí 6, bátsó máhà 7.. úwó 10, ece 20) plus a sociolinguistic note and 'number system is based on five'. Tone MARKS only -- no statement of the tone inventory, and nothing on stress/accent. Wordlist-only data.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. c. 2011. 'Jukunoid materials' web page, rogerblench.info/Language/Niger-Congo/BC/Jukunoid/JkOP.htm (Internet Archive copy 2012-11-14), plus the Internet Archive's index listings of the whole rogerblench.info site (all PDFs, all.doc files, Jukunoid and BC/General folders).
sources.note: Nothing; the page indexes only a Jibu dictionary and Kuteb grammar/photos. No Lufu (or Bete/Yukuben) wordlist or paper was ever posted on the archived site, contrary to the earlier scan's guess of a 'Koops 2007 Lufu word list' there. Live domain is now squatted.

sources.citation: Wichmann, Søren, Eric W. Holman & Cecil H. Brown (eds.). The ASJP Database. 'Wordlist Lufu' (doculect LUFU; ISO ldq, Glottocode lufu1237; compiled by Tessa de Mol-van Valen from Prischnegg, Tamara 2010, Zur Klassifikation 'Südjukunoider' Sprachen: lexikalische Evidenz, Afrika und Übersee 91: 87-118). Leipzig: MPI-EVA.
sources.note: 40-item Swadesh subset in ASJPcode (e.g. m 'I', u 'you', iSi 'we', uti 'one', bamaha 'two', ma 'person', ca 'fish', ti 'tree', Ti 'blood', mi 'water', la 'fire', ze 'name'); ASJPcode strips tone and stress, so the list carries no prosodic marking and no statement of any kind. Wordlist-only data; its value is as an open derivative of the print-only Prischnegg 2010 Lufu list.

sources.citation: Prischnegg, Tamara & John Rennison. 2007. Nigeria ganz anders – zwei Monate Sprachforschung bei den Jukun. In: Julia Ahamer & Gerda Lechleitner (Hrsg.), Um-Feld-Forschung: Erfahrungen – Erlebnisse – Ergebnisse, 283-296. Wien: Verlag der Oesterreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften. (Online edition ISBN 978-3-7001-3889-1, volume DOI 10.1553/0x00149a0e; TOC spells the first author 'Prischenegg'.)
sources.note: Nothing about Lufu prosody. The chapter is a fieldwork narrative (project aims, Yukuben sociolinguistics, the STx recording/segmentation reading, travel and equipment anecdotes). Its only linguistic-method remark touching tone is about Yukuben processing: STx 'berechnet.. die Frequenz der jeweiligen Äußerung. Das ist vor allem für die richtige Analyse des Tonmusters eine entscheidende Hilfe' (p.288-289) -- it presupposes tonal analysis of the recordings but states no tone system, and says nothing about stress/accent for any language. a full-text search for stress/accent Lufu = 1 hit; a full-t…

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2005. Is there a boundary between Plateau and Jukunoid? Paper for the Workshop on Jukunoid languages, Vienna, 15 November 2005. Draft, 27 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Lufu appears only on p.3 (sec. 1.3.2): 'Data on Oohum [=Yukuben] and other languages such as Bete and Lufu are surfacing from the Vienna project (Rennison et al., ined.)'. Phonology sections concern proto-Plateau; no stress statement for any Southern Jukunoid language.

sources.citation: Brenzinger, Matthias (ed.). 1992. Language Death: Factual and Theoretical Explorations with Special Reference to East Africa. (Contributions to the Sociology of Language 64.) Berlin; New York: Mouton de Gruyter. ISBN 3-11-013404-7. [copies we hold = the whole 456-page volume; target-language coverage is in Sommer, Gabriele, 'A survey on language death in Africa', pp. 301-417 (doi:10.1515/9783110870602.301), with minor mentions in Batibo, 'The fate of ethnic languages in Tanzania', pp. 85-98, and Legère, 'Language shift in Tanzania', pp. 99-115]

sources.note: Sociolinguistic questionnaire entry only (names, classification, status, speaker numbers, location, references); nothing on stress, accent or tone.

sources.citation: English Wikipedia, 'Lufu language' and 'Yukubenic languages' (wikitext via API).
sources.note: Stub: spoken mostly by older adults, speakers shifted to Jukun, close to Bete; no phonology.
